# alignment

```{r, engine='bash'}
/home/shared/hisat2-2.2.1/hisat2-build \
-f ../data/cgigas_uk_roslin_v1_genomic-mito.fa \
../output/cgigas_uk_roslin_v1_genomic-mito.index
```

```{r, engine='bash'}
/home/shared/hisat2-2.2.1/hisat2 \
-x ../output/cgigas_uk_roslin_v1_genomic-mito.index \
-p 32 \
-1 ../data/F143n08_R1_001.fastq.gz \
-2 ../data/F143n08_R2_001.fastq.gz \
-S ../output/F143_cgigas.sam
```



```{r, engine='bash'}
tail -1 ../output/F143_cgigas.sam
```



```{r, engine='bash'}
# Convert SAM to BAM, using 24 additional threads
/home/shared/samtools-1.12/samtools view -@ 24 -bS \
../output/F143_cgigas.sam > ../output/F143_cgigas.bam
```

```{r, engine='bash'}
# Sort the BAM file, using 12 additional threads
/home/shared/samtools-1.12/samtools sort -@ 12 \
../output/F143_cgigas.bam -o ../output/F143_cgigas_sorted.bam

# Index the sorted BAM file (multi-threading is not applicable to this operation)
/home/shared/samtools-1.12/samtools index \
../output/F143_cgigas_sorted.bam
```


# mpile-up



```{r, engine='bash'}
/home/shared/bcftools-1.14/bcftools mpileup --threads 24 --no-BAQ \
--fasta-ref ../data/cgigas_uk_roslin_v1_genomic-mito.fa \
../output/F143_cgigas_sorted.bam > ../output/F143_mpileup_output.txt
```

```{r, engine='bash'}
tail ../output/F143_mpileup_output.txt
```

```{r, engine='bash'}
cat ../output/F143_mpileup_output.txt \
| /home/shared/bcftools-1.14/bcftools call -mv -Oz \
> ../output/F143_mpile.vcf.gz
```


	•	bcftools call: calls genetic variants (SNPs/indels).
	•	-m: uses the multiallelic calling model (for multi-sample or complex sites).
	•	-v: outputs only variant sites (no reference sites).
	•	-Oz: outputs a compressed VCF (.vcf.gz), using bgzip.




```{r, engine='bash'}
zgrep "^##" -v ../output/F143_mpile.vcf.gz | \
awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} {split($8, a, ";"); print $1,$2,$4,$5,$6,a[1],$9,$10}' | tail

```

Step-by-Step:
	1.	zgrep "^##" -v ../output/F143_mpile.vcf.gz
	•	zgrep searches through a gzipped file.
	•	-v "^##" excludes lines that start with ##, which are the metadata header lines in a VCF.
	•	This allows column headers (#CHROM, etc.) and variant records through.
	2.	awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} {split($8, a, ";"); print $1,$2,$4,$5,$6,a[1],$9,$10}'
	•	Sets output field separator to tab.
	•	Splits the 8th column (the INFO field) by semicolons into array a.
	•	Then prints:
	•	$1 = CHROM
	•	$2 = POS
	•	$4 = REF
	•	$5 = ALT
	•	$6 = QUAL
	•	a[1] = the first INFO field tag (e.g., DP=123)
	•	$9 = FORMAT string
	•	$10 = sample genotype data

```{bash}
# Step 1: Unzip the file to a temporary file
zcat ../output/F143_mpile.vcf.gz | head -n -1 > ../output/F143_mpile_trimmed.vcf

# Step 2: Recompress the trimmed file
bgzip ../output/F143_mpile_trimmed.vcf

# Step 3: (Optional) Index the new file if needed
tabix -p vcf ../output/F143_mpile_trimmed.vcf.gz
```


The code below might not work. That is fine. The VCF in the above chunk can be used for visualization in IGV.

```{r, engine='bash'}
/home/shared/bcftools-1.14/bcftools call \
-v -c ../output/F143_mpile.vcf.gz \
> ../output/F143_mpile_calls.vcf
```
